Subject: Novacorp TCO postcall recap

Hi Emily,

Thanks for the call today — good alignment on goals. Quick recap and next steps below.

TL;DR
- Primary pain: token spend running conversational NPS assistant (~120M tokens/mo) + long contexts driving cost
- Goal: pilot by July, target p50 latency <250ms for core flows, keep pilot cost <= $15k/mo
- Ballpark TCO: current spend ~$18,000/mo; expected reduction to ~$11k–13k/mo with batching+caching+4-bit quantization

Pain points discussed:
- High token volume (peak QPS during support hours)
- Long average context length (~800 tokens) due to user histories
- Budget constraint: finance wants pilot <= $15k/month
- Need predictable latency for customer-facing flows

Redwood levers (how we get to the reduction):
1) Prefix/KV caching: cache repeated system prompts and recent context snippets. Expect 15–30% token reduction on core intents.
2) Smart batching: continuous batching for steady traffic windows—improves GPU utilization and reduces per-token compute by ~20–30%.
3) Model routing: route non-critical/low-sensitivity requests to a cheaper quantized variant.
4) 4-bit quantization: reduces GPU memory and increases throughput; combined with batching, improves cost efficiency.

Sample ballpark math (assumptions below):
- Current: 120M tokens/mo ≈ $18,000/mo
- With 25% caching hit + 25% batching gains + model routing/quantization: ~40% total TCO reduction -> ~$10.8k/mo
Assumptions: current effective per-token = $0.00015; caching hits 20–30%; batching gains depend on request distribution.

Requested artifacts / next steps:
- Emily: can you share 7 days of anonymized request logs (or the usage snapshot you mentioned)? (attachment stub: Novacorp-usage-snapshot-20260517.csv)
- Redwood: we'll produce a 2-page ballpark TCO and a pilot plan (attach by Tue 5/19)
- Schedule: technical deep dive (API/observability, KV cache integration) — propose Wed 6/2 10:00 AM PT

If it helps, we can run a 4-week pilot with a capped spend and a $5k onboarding credit to reduce risk. We'll include explicit metrics for cache hit rate, tokens saved, latency p50/p95, and a simple ROI calc tying fewer agent handoffs to agent cost savings.

Thanks — I'll follow up tomorrow with the ballpark PDF and a proposed mutual action plan.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Emily / Tom — thanks, note below is a short breakdown and pilot option. Attached: novacorp-tco-ballpark-20260519.pdf and a pilot SOW draft.

Ballpark breakdown (examples):
- Current effective rate: $0.00015/token -> 120M tokens = $18,000
- Caching: 25% effective token reduction on core intents -> saves 30M tokens
- Batching/throughput: 20% compute efficiency improvement -> equivalent to 24M token savings
- Quantized model & routing: further 10% effective reduction -> ~12M tokens
Total effective token reduction: ~40% -> net tokens billed ~72M -> estimated spend at our hosted rates ~$10.8k/mo

Guarantee/cap: we can offer a capped pilot SOW for $15k with defined success metrics. If actual usage exceeds the cap, Redwood will throttle non-critical routes or route to a lower-cost variant unless Novacorp approves overages. We will include clear observability hooks so procurement can see daily spend burn.

Pilot offer (4 weeks):
- Fixed cap: $15k
- Redwood credit/onboarding: $5k offset applied to the first invoice
- Deliverables: daily spend dashboard, cache-hit telemetry, p50/p95 latency, token-level cost breakdown
- Acceptance criteria: cache hit >=20% and p50 latency <=350ms for core flows, or we revisit optimizations

Next steps:
1) Emily: confirm you can share the logs by EOD Tue so we can finalize ballpark PDF
2) Ben/Marissa: can you review the attached PDF and SOW draft and prepare a pricing table we can share with Tom? (internal)
3) Book technical deep dive: propose Wed 6/2 10:00 AM PT — I’ll send a calendar invite

Thanks — I'll wait for the logs and will send an updated draft SOW by EOD today.
